results.title: Die Rolling & Opposite Face Deduction
results.prompt: A standard die has opposite faces summing to 7 (1 opposite 6, 2 opposite 5, 3 opposite 4). With 1 on top and 2 facing North, roll the die North once, then East once. What number is now on top?
results.reply: To figure this out, let's map the die in 3D space. If 1 is on top and 2 is facing North, then since opposite faces sum to 7, 6 is on the bottom and 5 is facing South. That leaves 3 and 4 for East and West; if we assume a standard right-handed die layout where 3 is East and 4 is West, rolling it North means the face that was facing South moves to the top. So, after the first roll North, 5 is on top. Then, rolling it East means the face that was facing West moves to the top. Since 4 was facing West, 4 is now on top.
